page.title: Binding registry
page.purpose: Answer two questions nothing else in Vrooli can answer: what can an agent actually call, and for everything it cannot, why not. The second half is the point — an unbound capability is a real gap in the acting surface even when the underlying capability plainly exists.

priorities.statement: Every unbound capability states its reason. A capability is never listed as unavailable without one.
priorities.notes: The reasons are a closed set — no manifest, local-only command, omitted RPC, external-tool-only. A capability that fits none of them is shown as unclassified, which is itself a finding, rather than being dropped from the list.

priorities.statement: The page carries information with an empty program corpus.
priorities.notes: This is why the surface was promoted out of OT-P2-001. On day one, before a single program has run, the registry is already the honest picture of the acting surface.

priorities.statement: Bound and unbound are shown against one another, never as separate inventories.
priorities.notes: A reader should be able to see the ratio without doing arithmetic. Manifest coverage is the ceiling on everything this scenario can do, and hiding the denominator would conceal that.

priorities.statement: A binding's declared effect and permissions are visible before anyone calls it.
priorities.notes: Governance is read from cli-manifest and never restated here. The page displays the contract; it does not author one.

priorities.statement: Reading the registry never mutates anything.
priorities.notes: Every surface on this page is a query. No affordance on it can submit a call.

states.description: The resolved namespace is browsable and unbound capabilities are listed with their reasons.
The registry is resolving from the descriptor image and the CLI manifests.
No manifest resolved at all, so nothing is callable. Distinct from a registry that resolved and found little.
The registry resolved but at least one manifest failed to parse; the affected scenarios are named and excluded rather than silently missing.
The descriptor image or a manifest changed since this registry snapshot was taken.
A filter or query is narrowing the namespace.
The registry could not be read and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Callable namespace
elements.description: The resolved surface, nested scenario > group > command, mirroring the path a program writes.

elements.name: Binding coverage
elements.description: Bound versus total operation classes, with the manifest-coverage denominator stated alongside.

elements.name: Unbound capabilities
elements.description: One entry per capability with no typed binding, each carrying its unbound reason.

elements.name: Unbound reason
elements.description: Which of the closed set applies: no manifest, local-only binding, omitted RPC, or external-tool-only.

elements.name: Unclassified capability
elements.description: Shown when a capability matches no declared unbound reason, so the gap in the taxonomy is visible rather than swallowed.

elements.name: Binding signature
elements.description: Typed request fields resolved from the proto descriptor.

elements.name: Declared effect
elements.description: read, write, or destructive, read from cli-manifest governance.

claims.statement: The page exposes a named registry region containing both the callable namespace and the unbound list.
No entry in the unbound list renders without an unbound reason or an explicit unclassified marker.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-007. A capability listed as unavailable with no reason is indistinguishable from a bug in the registry, and teaches operators to distrust the whole surface.

claims.statement: The coverage summary shows the denominator alongside the bound count, including how many scenarios ship no manifest at all.
claims.rationale: Manifest coverage is the hard ceiling on the acting surface. A bound count without its denominator reads as completeness.

claims.statement: The registry renders its full information with zero programs in the corpus.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-007's promotion argument. If this page needs program history to be useful, it belongs back at P2.

claims.statement: A registry that resolved nothing is visibly different from one that resolved with some manifests failing.
A binding's declared effect is conveyed by text as well as by any color treatment.
claims.rationale: destructive versus read is the distinction that decides whether a grant is needed; it must not depend on color perception.

claims.statement: No affordance on this page submits a call or mutates state.
claims.rationale: The registry is a query surface. An execute affordance here would create a submission path with no session, no grant, and no provenance.

claims.statement: When the descriptor image or a manifest has changed since the snapshot, the page says so rather than presenting stale data as current.
claims.rationale: A stale registry silently misreports what an agent can call, which is worse than reporting unavailable.

claims.statement: Loading, empty, partial, stale, searching, and error states each render dedicated content.
The namespace tree, the filter, and every unbound entry are reachable by keyboard alone.
